A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AAA-Gaussians and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D. Matching the text and rendered pages supports comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction metrics, component ablations, rendering robustness tests, and runtime measurements in Tables 1–5, plus per-scene results and visual comparisons in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds large-field-of-view results for two comparison methods in Table 3.

M1.justification: The adaptive 3D smoothing filter, view-space bounding, frustum-based culling, and hierarchical sorting remain unchanged. The added Section 3 overview explains existing components without changing their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 13 scenes from Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending. Standard views, enlarged field of view, multiresolution rendering, and close-camera scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Mip-Splatting and Taming 3DGS to the large-field-of-view comparison, which previously included only 3DGS, StopThePop, and MCMC alongside the proposed method. Both additions already appeared in the standard-view comparison; other comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported preprocessing, densification settings, primitive-count controls, metrics, resolution levels, and runtime measurement procedures are unchanged. Table 3 retains the protocol of dividing focal length by three and multiplying resolution by three.

E4.justification: The existing large-field-of-view robustness analysis gains evidence for Mip-Splatting and Taming 3DGS, extending the comparison of resistance to projection artifacts. Component ablations, multiresolution tests, timing analyses, and appendix examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both describe the same averaging of rendering timings over an interpolated camera path.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS results for Mip-Splatting and Taming 3DGS across all three datasets. For example, their Tanks & Temples PSNR values are 17.314 and 11.545, respectively, versus the unchanged 23.583 for the proposed method. Existing numerical results, including Appendix Table 6 and figure inset scores, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–26 and the amplitude-scaling and bounding derivations in Appendices A–B retain the same mathematical content. Differences in equation typesetting and placement do not introduce or correct mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of unified artifact-free real-time rendering, competitive standard-view quality, and robustness to out-of-distribution views. The added comparisons support existing claims without broadening them.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly states that frustum-based culling improves performance without affecting reconstruction quality. Section 3.1 removes the explanation that training naturally adapts to maximum-contribution evaluation. The applicability limitations in Section 5 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly announces publicly available training and rendering source code and supplies a repository link in the introduction. v1 has no corresponding access statement. Implementation settings and hardware disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Celarek et al.'s work on accurate volumetric rendering and Tu et al.'s VRSplat, while removing Wyman's OIT citation and associated discussion. These are limited updates; the positioning as a unified artifact-removal framework remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits and condenses related work and preliminaries, adds a method overview, and includes acknowledgments and an additional author affiliation. The main section sequence, appendix organization, and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 adds artifact-indicator columns and reorders ablation rows. Table 3 expands for the added comparators but duplicates the Mip-Splatting row in its first block. Figures retain their content, with limited caption, spacing, and page-flow adjustments.

improvement.justification: The additional Table 3 comparisons modestly strengthen support for the existing robustness claim, while the code-access statement and method overview improve reproducibility guidance and clarity. These benefits outweigh the limited presentation defect of the duplicated Mip-Splatting row. The method, theory, and most evidence remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
